meanings: to set one's mind at rest
to keep one's mind on sth

components.note: 宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 知道飞机安全降落，她终于安心了。
example.pinyin: Zhīdào fēijī ānquán jiàngluò, tā zhōngyú ānxīn le.
example.english: Knowing the plane had landed safely, she finally felt relieved.
example.fact: Commercial aviation is statistically one of the safest ways to travel: the global fatal-accident rate has fallen to a few per ten million flights, thanks largely to redundant systems, collision-avoidance technology, and rigorous crew training. Modern jetliners are also engineered to glide safely for many kilometers even after a complete loss of engine power, giving pilots time to reach a runway.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 淹 describes being covered by water.
奄 (yǎn) is close in sound to yān, sharing the same initial.
匕 (a kneeling person) — a mourner bowed down in grief.
歹 (skeletal remains) — the corpse being mourned, the source of 死's meaning 'to die, dead.'

example.hanzi: 那个男孩差点在河里淹死。
example.pinyin: Nàge nánhái chàdiǎn zài hé lǐ yānsǐ.
example.english: That boy nearly drowned in the river.
example.fact: The mammalian dive reflex slows a person's heart rate and redirects blood toward vital organs the moment the face is submerged in cold water, a response that is strongest in infants. It is one reason some cold-water drowning victims, especially children, have been successfully resuscitated after unusually long periods underwater.

meanings: benefit (provided by an employer or organization)

components.note: 礻 (spirit/altar) — 福 relates to blessings granted by the spirits
畐 (fú) matches the sound of 福's reading fú exactly.
禾 (grain, a growing rice or wheat plant) — 利 pictures a harvest.
刂 (knife) — cutting grain at harvest time was a clear benefit or gain, giving 利 its meaning 'profit' or 'advantage.'

example.hanzi: 这家公司为员工提供很好的福利。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī wèi yuángōng tígōng hěn hǎo de fúlì.
example.english: This company provides very good benefits for its employees.
example.fact: Germany introduced the world's first modern social-insurance system in the 1880s under Chancellor Otto von Bismarck, combining sickness, accident, and old-age insurance funded jointly by workers and employers. The model spread across Europe over the following decades and became a template for later national welfare programs, including the U.S. Social Security system created in 1935.

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赛 originally related to offering valuables, later coming to mean 'to compete.'
宀 (mián) is only distantly related in sound to sài, the connection having drifted apart over time.
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 他梦想有一天能拥有一辆赛车。
example.pinyin: Tā mèngxiǎng yǒu yī tiān néng yǒngyǒu yī liàng sàichē.
example.english: He dreams of one day owning a race car.
example.fact: Formula 1 cars generate so much aerodynamic downforce that, in theory, one could drive upside down through a tunnel at racing speed — the airflow beneath and around the car pushes it into the track hard enough to counteract gravity above roughly 130 kilometers per hour.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
犭 (dog) on the left represents a guard dog.
讠 (speech) suggests an accusation or a legal case being spoken.
犬 (dog) on the right completes the scene, giving 狱 its meaning 'prison, lawsuit.'

example.hanzi: 他因表现良好提前出狱了。
example.pinyin: Tā yīn biǎoxiàn liánghǎo tíqián chūyù le.
example.english: He was released from prison early for good behavior.
example.fact: Nelson Mandela was released from South Africa's Victor Verster Prison on 11 February 1990 after 27 years of incarceration, walking free before a global television audience. Four years later he became South Africa's first democratically elected president.

components.note: 宀 (a roof) — a house where valuables are kept
玉 (jade) — the treasure kept safe inside
艹 (grass) — 藏 relates to hiding something among vegetation.
臧 (zāng) is close in rhyme to cáng, sharing a similar initial.

example.hanzi: 探险队在山洞深处发现了一批宝藏。
example.pinyin: Tànxiǎnduì zài shāndòng shēnchù fāxiàn le yī pī bǎozàng.
example.english: The expedition team discovered a trove of treasure deep inside the cave.
example.fact: In 2009 a metal detectorist in a Staffordshire farm field unearthed the largest hoard of Anglo-Saxon gold ever found — more than 3,500 items, mostly war gear, dating to around the 7th century AD. The Staffordshire Hoard is now valued at over three million pounds and displayed in museums in Birmingham and Stoke-on-Trent.

components.note: 田 (field, farm) — livestock are raised on a farm.
玄 (xuán) is only distantly related in sound to chù, the connection having drifted apart over time.
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.

example.hanzi: 农场里养着各种畜生，比如牛和羊。
example.pinyin: Nóngchǎng lǐ yǎng zhe gèzhǒng chùsheng, bǐrú niú hé yáng.
example.english: The farm keeps all kinds of livestock, such as cattle and sheep.
example.fact: Cattle were domesticated from wild aurochs roughly 10,500 years ago in the Near East, and genetic studies show nearly all modern cattle breeds descend from a surprisingly small founding population of around 80 female aurochs. The aurochs itself survived in the wild until 1627, when the last known individual died in Poland's Jaktorów Forest.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — the living thing in bloom.
化 (transformation) — the plant changing into blossom, the source of 花's meaning 'flower.'
贝 (shell/money) — 费 relates to spending money, fees, and expenses
弗 (fú) has only a loose sound connection to 费's reading fèi

example.hanzi: 装修这套房子花费了他们大量的时间和金钱。
example.pinyin: Zhuāngxiū zhè tào fángzi huāfèi le tāmen dàliàng de shíjiān hé jīnqián.
example.english: Renovating this apartment cost them a great deal of time and money.
example.fact: The Sydney Opera House was originally budgeted at about 7 million Australian dollars and estimated to take four years to build; it ended up costing roughly 102 million dollars and took fourteen years, opening in 1973. Its architect, Jørn Utzon, resigned from the project in 1966 and never saw the finished building in person.

components.note: 上 (top) — the upper edge pressing down
卜 — the lower edge, with a card squeezed between the two
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) is close in sound to tè, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 卡特总统在任期内积极推动人权外交。
example.pinyin: Kǎtè zǒngtǒng zài rènqī nèi jījí tuīdòng rénquán wàijiāo.
example.english: President Carter actively promoted human-rights diplomacy during his term.
example.fact: Jimmy Carter, the 39th U.S. president, lived to 100 years old, longer than any other former U.S. president in history, and died in December 2024. After leaving office in 1981 he spent decades building homes with Habitat for Humanity and helped negotiate the 1978 Camp David Accords, for which he later received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2002.

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) is a related sound to xìng, though the initial has shifted over time.
马 (horse) sets the scene — an animal being pestered.
蚤 (flea) sits beside it — a flea biting and irritating a horse, giving 骚 its meaning 'to disturb, to harass.'
扌 (hand) — 扰 describes stirring something up by hand, 'to disturb.'
尤 (yóu) is only distantly related in sound to rǎo — the connection has drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 公司专门设立了举报性骚扰的渠道。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī zhuānmén shèlì le jǔbào xìng sāorǎo de qúdào.
example.english: The company set up a dedicated channel for reporting sexual harassment.
example.fact: The term "sexual harassment" was popularized in the United States in the mid-1970s by a group of women at Cornell University, and the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission did not formally recognize it as a form of illegal sex discrimination until 1980. The phrase "Me Too" itself was coined by activist Tarana Burke in 2006, more than a decade before it went viral globally in 2017.

components.note: 大 (a person) at the top represents someone leading.
冖 (a rope or cover shape) in the middle shows a tether.
牛 (ox) at the bottom is the animal being led, giving 牵 its meaning 'to lead by hand, to pull.'
扌 (hand) — 扯 describes pulling or tearing something by hand.
止 (zhǐ) is only distantly related in sound to 扯's reading chě, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这起案件牵扯到好几家公司。
example.pinyin: Zhè qǐ ànjiàn qiānchě dào hǎo jǐ jiā gōngsī.
example.english: This case involves several companies.
example.fact: The 2015 Volkswagen "Dieselgate" emissions scandal eventually implicated multiple automakers across the industry after investigators found software designed to cheat pollution tests. Volkswagen alone has paid more than 30 billion euros in fines, buybacks, and settlements worldwide since the scandal broke.

components.note: Bird — an older semantic root kept from the character's structure.
Is close in sound to zhōu, related to diāo but drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) matches the sound of 像's reading xiàng exactly.

example.hanzi: 广场中央立着一座巨大的雕像。
example.pinyin: Guǎngchǎng zhōngyāng lì zhe yī zuò jùdà de diāoxiàng.
example.english: A huge statue stands in the middle of the square.
example.fact: Michelangelo's marble statue of David, completed in 1504, stands over 5.17 meters tall and was carved from a single block of Carrara marble that two earlier sculptors had already abandoned as flawed decades before. Its head and hands are deliberately oversized relative to its body, a technique thought to compensate for the original plan to display it high on a cathedral roofline it never reached.

meanings: start explaining and it's a long story
complicated and not easy to express succinctly

components.note: 讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.

example.hanzi: 我们怎么认识的？说来话长。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zěnme rènshi de? Shuōláihuàcháng.
example.english: How did we meet? It's a long story.
example.fact: The Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic poem, is roughly ten times the combined length of Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, running to about 200,000 verse lines — making it one of the longest single literary works ever composed within a single tradition.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 没 originally meant to sink or drown in water, later extended to the negative 'not have.'
殳 (shū) is the historical sound component; it no longer rhymes with méi in modern Mandarin, another case of sound drift over time.
穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) is close in sound to kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 我今天没空，我们改天再聊吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān méi kòng, wǒmen gǎitiān zài liáo ba.
example.english: I don't have time today; let's talk another day.
example.fact: Switzerland's national rail operator, SBB, runs one of the most punctual networks in the world, with roughly 90% of trains arriving within three minutes of schedule — a feat achieved partly because the entire national timetable is coordinated to the minute across every connecting line.

components.note: 爪 and 彐 (two hands, reaching from opposite sides) — a simplified form of 爭, grabbing for the same thing.
亅 (the object) — what the two hands are struggling over, giving 争 its meaning 'to contend, compete, fight for.'
扌 (hand) — a hand gripping something tightly
丸 (a pebble/pellet) — the small object held firmly in the hand

example.hanzi: 两位邻居因为停车位发生了争执。
example.pinyin: Liǎng wèi línjū yīnwèi tíngchēwèi fāshēng le zhēngzhí.
example.english: The two neighbors got into a dispute over a parking spot.
example.fact: Bir Tawil, a roughly 2,060-square-kilometer patch of desert between Egypt and Sudan, is one of the few pieces of land on Earth that no country claims — both nations disavow it because claiming it would mean giving up their claim to the more valuable, disputed Hala'ib Triangle nearby.

components.note: Step/walk — following a path.
Is close in sound to dùn, related to xún but drifted apart over time.
王 (a variant of 玉, jade) — 环 originally referred to a round jade ring or bracelet
不 (bù) is only distantly related in sound to 环's reading huán, having drifted apart considerably over time

example.hanzi: 水在自然界中不断循环。
example.pinyin: Shuǐ zài zìránjiè zhōng bùduàn xúnhuán.
example.english: Water continuously cycles through nature.
example.fact: A single water molecule spends an average of about nine days in Earth's atmosphere before falling back down as precipitation, but it can remain locked in polar ice sheets or deep groundwater for thousands of years. The same water molecules cycling through today's rain have likely been recycled through the atmosphere and oceans countless times since the planet's oceans formed.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
日 (sun) — represents the sun.
十 depicts the first rays of sunlight appearing low on the horizon — together with 日 (sun) giving 早 its meaning 'early, morning.'

example.hanzi: 他一早就出发去机场了。
example.pinyin: Tā yīzǎo jiù chūfā qù jīchǎng le.
example.english: He set off for the airport early in the morning.
example.fact: Benjamin Franklin was a famous early riser who claimed to wake at 5 a.m. and outlined an idealized daily schedule in his autobiography. Modern chronobiology research, however, shows that a person's natural sleep-wake preference is largely genetic, so 'morning lark' versus 'night owl' tendencies are not simply a matter of willpower.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 探 describes reaching out with the hand to search for something.
糸 (thread) — thick strands twisted into a rope
冖 (a covering) — the ceiling or beam the rope hangs from

example.hanzi: 科学家们不断探索宇宙的奥秘。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen bùduàn tànsuǒ yǔzhòu de àomì.
example.english: Scientists continually explore the mysteries of the universe.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched by NASA in 1977, is now the most distant human-made object from Earth, having crossed into interstellar space in 2012. It is currently more than 24 billion kilometers away and still transmits data back to Earth, though its plutonium power source is expected to run too low to operate any instruments by around 2025.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 停 relates to a person coming to a halt
亭 (tíng) matches the sound of 停's reading tíng exactly
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 裁判喊了一声，两名拳手立刻停手。
example.pinyin: Cáipàn hǎn le yī shēng, liǎng míng quánshǒu lìkè tíngshǒu.
example.english: The referee shouted, and the two boxers stopped immediately.
example.fact: In professional boxing, a referee can stop a fight through a technical knockout even without a boxer being knocked down, if they are deemed unable to safely continue. The mechanism was formalized in the early 20th century after several in-ring deaths pushed boxing commissions to give referees stronger authority to halt dangerous or mismatched bouts.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 驱 describes spurring a horse onward, extending to 'to drive, to expel.'
区 (qū) matches the sound of 驱 exactly.
辶 (to walk) — 逐 means to chase or pursue, involving movement.
豕 (shǐ) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading zhú has diverged.

example.hanzi: 那个国家驱逐了一批外国记者。
example.pinyin: Nàge guójiā qūzhú le yī pī wàiguó jìzhě.
example.english: That country expelled a group of foreign journalists.
example.fact: In 1609, Spain expelled hundreds of thousands of Moriscos — Muslims who had converted to Christianity — in one of the largest forced population movements in early modern European history, reshaping the demographics of entire regions of southern Spain within just a few years.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — relates directly to 病's meaning 'illness, disease, to be sick.'
丙 (bǐng) shares its base sound with bìng, differing only in tone.
户 (door) — 房 relates to a room or house, a space behind a door
方 (fāng) is close in sound to 房's reading fáng

example.hanzi: 护士每小时都会来病房检查病人。
example.pinyin: Hùshi měi xiǎoshí dōu huì lái bìngfáng jiǎnchá bìngrén.
example.english: The nurse comes to the ward to check on patients every hour.
example.fact: Florence Nightingale's statistical work during the Crimean War in the 1850s showed that far more soldiers were dying of preventable infections in unsanitary hospital wards than of battle wounds. Her push for cleaner facilities and better ventilation helped found the modern field of hospital epidemiology.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
A drawing of a robe's collar and folded sides, seen from the front.

example.hanzi: 天气变冷了，她穿上了厚厚的大衣。
example.pinyin: Tiānqì biàn lěng le, tā chuān shàng le hòuhòu de dàyī.
example.english: The weather turned cold, so she put on a thick overcoat.
example.fact: Merino sheep wool fibers are naturally crimped and can absorb roughly 30% of their weight in moisture while still keeping the wearer feeling dry, which is why wool coats and base layers remain effective insulators for polar explorers even in freezing, humid conditions where synthetic fabrics can fail.

components.note: 亻 (a person) — someone receiving something
寸 (a hand) — a hand handing something over
纟 (thread/silk) — 给 originally related to supplying thread or material, later broadening to mean 'to give.'
合 (hé) is close in sound to 给's reading gěi, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 公司每月按时把工资付给员工。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī měi yuè ànshí bǎ gōngzī fùgěi yuángōng.
example.english: The company pays employees' salaries on time every month.
example.fact: Some of the oldest surviving payroll records come from ancient Mesopotamia, where workers building temples and canals around 3000 BC were paid in rations of barley beer. A typical laborer received about two liters a day, with the amount recorded on cuneiform tablets scaling with rank, similar to a modern pay grade.

components.note: 尺 (a ruler/measure) — represents rules or measures being set.
口 (mouth) — measures being discussed aloud in one place gave 局 its meaning 'bureau, office, situation.'
力 (strength) — 势 relates to power, force, and influence
执 (zhí) has only a loose sound connection to 势's reading shì

example.hanzi: 分析师密切关注着国际局势的变化。
example.pinyin: Fēnxīshī mìqiè guānzhù zhe guójì júshì de biànhuà.
example.english: Analysts are closely watching changes in the international situation.
example.fact: During the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis, the world came arguably closer to nuclear war than at any other point in history. Declassified records later revealed that Soviet submarine officer Vasili Arkhipov was one of three men required to authorize a nuclear torpedo launch and was the lone dissenting vote that prevented it.

components.note: 冖 here is a distorted form of 力 (strength) — a simplified way of showing soldiers grouped together.
车 (cart/vehicle) — 军 originally pictured soldiers riding out to battle in war chariots.

士 was originally a pictograph of a broad, upright axe or adze — a tool once carried as a mark of authority. Wielding it came to signify a capable man, giving 士 its meaning 'scholar, gentleman, soldier.'

example.hanzi: 那位军士负责训练新兵。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi jūnshì fùzé xùnliàn xīnbīng.
example.english: That noncommissioned officer is in charge of training new recruits.
example.fact: The rank structure separating commissioned officers from noncommissioned officers dates back to the Roman legions, where centurions — promoted from the ranks rather than appointed by birth or political connection — commanded roughly 80 soldiers each and were prized for battlefield experience rather than social standing.

components.note: 氵 (water) — relates to 清's meaning 'clear (water), pure.'
青 (qīng) matches the sound of 清 exactly.
氵 (water) — 洗 describes cleaning something with water.
先 (xiān) shares the initial x- with xǐ, though the rhyme has drifted.

example.hanzi: 医生反复叮嘱要用肥皂彻底清洗双手。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng fǎnfù dīngzhǔ yào yòng féizào chèdǐ qīngxǐ shuāngshǒu.
example.english: The doctor repeatedly reminded people to thoroughly wash their hands with soap.
example.fact: In the 1840s, Hungarian physician Ignaz Semmelweis discovered that hospital deaths from childbed fever dropped dramatically when doctors washed their hands with a chlorinated lime solution before examining patients. His idea was rejected by most of his medical peers during his lifetime, and it took decades for handwashing to become standard medical practice.

meanings: woman of senior authority in a household

components.note: 丶 (a dot) — represents the burning flame atop a lamp.
王 here depicts the base and stand of an oil lamp, not its usual meaning 'king' — the one who tends the flame became linked to 'master, lord, main.'
女 (woman) forms the left side of the character.
彐 depicts a broom — a woman holding a broom, a traditional image of housework, gave 妇 its meaning 'married woman, wife.'

example.hanzi: 她是一位全职主妇，把家里打理得井井有条。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yī wèi quánzhí zhǔfù, bǎ jiā lǐ dǎlǐ de jǐngjǐngyǒutiáo.
example.english: She is a full-time housewife who keeps the household perfectly organized.
example.fact: Economists who try to estimate the market value of unpaid household work — cooking, cleaning, and childcare — have found it would add trillions of dollars a year to major economies if it were counted in GDP. OECD estimates put the value of unpaid household work at roughly 20 to 60 percent of measured GDP, depending on the country.

components.note: 贝 (shell) — ancient Chinese currency was made from cowrie shells, linking 贝 to wealth
才 (cái) matches the sound of 财's reading cái exactly
力 (strength, effort) at the bottom — 务 relates to a task requiring effort, giving it the meaning 'affairs, business, to be engaged in.'
The upper part is a simplified trace of 敄, the phonetic element in the traditional form 務, and is close in sound to 务's reading wù.

example.hanzi: 她负责公司的财务工作。
example.pinyin: Tā fùzé gōngsī de cáiwù gōngzuò.
example.english: She is in charge of the company's financial affairs.
example.fact: Double-entry bookkeeping, the accounting method still used by virtually every modern business, was first systematically described in 1494 by Italian friar and mathematician Luca Pacioli in a mathematics textbook, centuries before accounting became a distinct profession.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 菜 names something grown, a vegetable.
采 (cǎi) is close in sound to cài, differing only in tone.
单 (simplified from 單) depicts a two-pronged hunting tool, such as a slingshot or forked weapon, bound to a handle — the source of 单's meaning 'single, only, sheet, list.'

example.hanzi: 服务员递给我们一份菜单。
example.pinyin: Fúwùyuán dì gěi wǒmen yī fèn càidān.
example.english: The waiter handed us a menu.
example.fact: The printed restaurant menu is often traced to Paris in the years after the French Revolution, when many chefs who had cooked for aristocratic households lost their positions and opened public restaurants, listing dishes and prices on paper for a general paying clientele for the first time.

components.note: 业 (simplified from 業) depicts a large wooden board with a jagged top, once used as a stand for hanging bells and chime-stones during ritual performances — later broadened to mean 'trade, occupation, achievement.'
力 (strength, effort) at the bottom — 务 relates to a task requiring effort, giving it the meaning 'affairs, business, to be engaged in.'
The upper part is a simplified trace of 敄, the phonetic element in the traditional form 務, and is close in sound to 务's reading wù.

example.hanzi: 这家银行的业务范围很广。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā yínháng de yèwù fànwéi hěn guǎng.
example.english: This bank's scope of business is very broad.
example.fact: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena, founded in Siena, Italy in 1472, is recognized as the world's oldest bank still in operation, having survived plagues, wars, and multiple financial crises across more than five centuries of continuous business.

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 怪 relates to a feeling of surprise, unease, or strangeness.
圣 here is a phonetic component unrelated to its other reading shèng ('sacred'); it is close in sound to guài, a connection that has drifted apart over time.
⺼ (flesh) — 胎 originally named an unborn child inside the body.
台 (tái) is close in sound to tāi, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 那部电影里的怪胎其实心地善良。
example.pinyin: Nà bù diànyǐng lǐ de guàitāi qíshí xīndì shànliáng.
example.english: The "freak" character in that movie is actually kind-hearted.
example.fact: Conjoined twins occur in roughly one out of every 200,000 live births and result when a single fertilized egg only partially separates into two embryos during early development, typically between the 13th and 15th day after conception — a narrow window that determines whether, and how much, the twins remain joined.

components.note: 页 (head) is the semantic root here, though the exact link to 顺's meaning 'to follow' isn't fully clear today.
川 (chuān) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading shùn has diverged.
广 (a wide building) — 序 relates to arrangement, as in the ordered layout of a hall.
予 (yǔ) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though it has diverged from the modern reading xù.

example.hanzi: 请按照字母顺序排列这些名字。
example.pinyin: Qǐng ànzhào zìmǔ shùnxù páiliè zhèxiē míngzi.
example.english: Please arrange these names in alphabetical order.
example.fact: Alphabetical ordering as an organizing principle dates back at least to the Library of Alexandria in the 3rd century BC, where librarian Callimachus is credited with cataloguing works by author name in alphabetical sequence — one of the earliest known uses of the system still used in dictionaries and indexes today.

components.note: 木 (tree) — lemon (柠檬) grows on a tree.
宁 (níng) matches the sound of 柠 exactly.
木 (tree) — 檬 originally named a type of tree, later reused phonetically for 'lemon.'
蒙 (méng) matches the sound of 檬's reading exactly.

example.hanzi: 她在茶里加了一片柠檬。
example.pinyin: Tā zài chá lǐ jiā le yī piàn níngméng.
example.english: She added a slice of lemon to her tea.
example.fact: In 1747, Scottish naval surgeon James Lind conducted one of the first controlled clinical trials in medical history, showing that sailors who ate citrus fruits like lemons and oranges recovered from scurvy far faster than those given other remedies — decades before vitamin C was even identified as the active ingredient.

components.note: A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.

example.hanzi: 公司必须先解决自身的问题才能扩张。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī bìxū xiān jiějué zìshēn de wèntí cáinéng kuòzhāng.
example.english: The company must first solve its own problems before it can expand.
example.fact: The human body replaces the vast majority of its cells on a regular cycle — red blood cells last about four months, skin cells shed and regenerate roughly every two to four weeks — so most of the atoms making up a person's body today were not part of it a decade ago, even though a sense of continuous selfhood persists.

components.note: Mountain — the character describes a landform between mountains.
Shows a shape squeezed between two sides, suggesting a gorge.
八-shaped strokes at the top picture the sloping walls of a valley.
口 below pictures a spring or opening where water flows out, giving 谷 its meaning 'valley.'

example.hanzi: 他们徒步穿越了那条壮观的峡谷。
example.pinyin: Tāmen túbù chuānyuè le nà tiáo zhuàngguān de xiágǔ.
example.english: They hiked through that spectacular canyon.
example.fact: The Grand Canyon in Arizona is roughly 446 kilometers long and up to 1,857 meters deep, carved almost entirely by the Colorado River over the past five to six million years — a geologically short time span that has exposed nearly two billion years of Earth's rock layers along its walls.

components.note: 冂 traces the outer outline of a cut of meat.
仌 depicts the muscle fibers or ribs inside, together forming a picture of a piece of meat.
亻 (person) — 体 relates to the human body.
本 (běn) is close in sound to 体's reading tǐ, though the connection has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 长期缺乏运动会让肉体变得虚弱。
example.pinyin: Chángqī quēfá yùndòng huì ràng ròutǐ biàn de xūruò.
example.english: Long-term lack of exercise can make the physical body weak.
example.fact: Astronauts on long-duration missions can lose up to 20% of their muscle mass and significant bone density within just a few months in microgravity, since muscles and bones no longer have to work against gravity — which is why ISS crew members exercise roughly two hours a day using specialized resistance equipment.

meanings: (of celestial bodies etc) to move along one's course
(of a train service etc) to operate

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 运's meaning 'to move, transport,' and by extension 'fortune,' the movement of one's life.
云 (yún) shares its base sound with yùn, a difference only in tone.
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.

example.hanzi: 这条地铁线路每天早上五点开始运行。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo dìtiě xiànlù měitiān zǎoshàng wǔ diǎn kāishǐ yùnxíng.
example.english: This subway line starts operating at 5 a.m. every day.
example.fact: The London Underground, which opened in 1863, is the world's oldest underground railway system and initially ran on steam-powered locomotives through tunnels filled with smoke and soot, decades before electric trains were introduced on the network in the 1890s.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 运's meaning 'to move, transport,' and by extension 'fortune,' the movement of one's life.
云 (yún) shares its base sound with yùn, a difference only in tone.
车 (cart) — 输 originally meant to transport goods by cart.
俞 (yú) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading shū has diverged.

example.hanzi: 这些货物需要用大型卡车运输。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē huòwù xūyào yòng dàxíng kǎchē yùnshū.
example.english: These goods need to be transported by large trucks.
example.fact: The modern steel shipping container, standardized globally in the 1960s, is often credited with cutting the cost of international trade so dramatically that it reshaped the world economy — loading a ship went from days of manual labor per port call to just hours with cranes, letting a single large container ship now carry the equivalent of over 20,000 truckloads of cargo.

components.note: 豸 (a beast) suggests physical form.
皃 (an old form meaning 'face, appearance') combines with the beast radical, giving 貌 its meaning 'appearance, looks.'
亻 (a person), shown twice — one person next to another, similar in shape, the source of 似's meaning 'to resemble, similar, like.'

example.hanzi: 这道题貌似很简单，其实暗藏陷阱。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào tí màosì hěn jiǎndān, qíshí àncáng xiànjǐng.
example.english: This problem appears to be simple, but it actually hides a trap.
example.fact: The mimic octopus, discovered off Indonesia in the 1990s, can impersonate the appearance and movement of more than a dozen other sea creatures — including venomous lionfish and sea snakes — by changing its shape, color, and swimming pattern, likely to deter predators that avoid those more dangerous animals.

components.note: 林 here depicts eyes shut in sleep, not its usual meaning 'forest.'
夕 (evening, night) — sleeping at night is when dreams occur, giving 梦 its meaning 'dream.'
冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'

example.hanzi: 昨晚我梦见自己在天上飞。
example.pinyin: Zuówǎn wǒ mèngjiàn zìjǐ zài tiān shàng fēi.
example.english: Last night I dreamed I was flying through the sky.
example.fact: Most vivid dreaming occurs during REM sleep, a stage discovered in 1953 by researchers at the University of Chicago who noticed rapid eye movements and irregular brain activity in sleeping subjects. The body also becomes almost completely paralyzed during REM sleep, a state called atonia thought to prevent people from physically acting out their dreams.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 终 originally referred to the end of a woven thread, extended to mean 'end, final'
冬 (dōng) has only a loose sound connection to 终's reading zhōng
止 depicts a footprint, with toes at the top and the leg below — a simple picture of a foot, later extended to mean 'to stop.'

example.hanzi: 双方决定终止这项合作协议。
example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng juédìng zhōngzhǐ zhè xiàng hézuò xiéyì.
example.english: Both parties decided to terminate the cooperation agreement.
example.fact: NASA's Space Shuttle program was officially terminated in 2011 after 135 missions over 30 years, following the loss of two orbiters — Challenger in 1986 and Columbia in 2003 — with the decision driven partly by the high cost of extending the aging fleet's certified service life.

components.note: 木 (wood) — early models and molds were often carved from wood
莫 (mò) is close in sound to 模's reading mó, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
木 (tree/wood) — 样 originally referred to a kind of tree, later broadening to mean 'kind, appearance, way.'
羊 (yáng) matches the sound of 样's reading yàng, aside from tone.

example.hanzi: 多年不见，他的模样几乎没变。
example.pinyin: Duō nián bù jiàn, tā de múyàng jīhū méi biàn.
example.english: After many years apart, his appearance has barely changed.
example.fact: Researchers who study facial aging have found that the human face keeps its recognizable proportions for decades mainly because bone structure changes little after growth stops around age 20. Most visible aging comes instead from soft-tissue and skin changes — fat redistribution, collagen loss, and gravity's gradual pull — rather than the skeleton reshaping itself.

meanings: (of a document etc) to be uploaded to the Internet
(tennis, volleyball etc) to move in close to the net

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
网 depicts a woven mesh net stretched over a frame — a picture of a fishing or hunting net, giving 网 its meaning 'net, network.'

example.hanzi: 现在几乎每个人每天都要上网。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài jīhū měi gèrén měitiān dōu yào shàngwǎng.
example.english: Nowadays almost everyone goes online every day.
example.fact: The first message ever sent over what became the Internet was transmitted in 1969 between computers at UCLA and Stanford Research Institute. The system crashed after just two letters of the word "login" were typed, making "lo" the accidental first message in internet history.

meanings: China north of the Yellow River

components.note: 匕 (a person), doubled and mirrored — two people standing back-to-back; this shape was later reused to write the unrelated directional meaning 'north.'
方 was originally a pictograph — likely of a plow blade, or of two boats lashed side by side — later extended to mean 'square, direction, method.'

example.hanzi: 冬天北方常常大雪纷飞。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān běifāng chángcháng dàxuě fēnfēi.
example.english: In winter, heavy snow often falls in the north.
example.fact: Earth's magnetic north pole is not fixed — it has been drifting from northern Canada toward Siberia at speeds that increased to roughly 50 to 60 kilometers per year in recent decades, forcing scientists to update the World Magnetic Model used by compasses, ships, and smartphone navigation more frequently than planned.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plant) — 葡 relates to a climbing plant, the grapevine.
匍 (pú) matches the sound of 葡 exactly.
艹 (grass, plant) — 萄 relates to a climbing plant, the grapevine.
匋 (táo) matches the sound of 萄 exactly.
酉 (a wine jar) — the vessel holding the drink
氵 (liquid) — the wine itself inside the jar

example.hanzi: 晚餐时他们开了一瓶红葡萄酒。
example.pinyin: Wǎncān shí tāmen kāi le yī píng hóng pútáojiǔ.
example.english: They opened a bottle of red wine at dinner.
example.fact: Archaeologists have found chemical residue of wine in pottery jars from the Republic of Georgia dating back roughly 8,000 years, making it some of the earliest evidence of winemaking yet discovered — long before wine culture became associated with ancient Greece and Rome.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 制 relates to cutting and shaping, and by extension, to making or controlling something.
巾 (jīn) is close in sound to zhì, a connection that has drifted over time.
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 政府正在制定新的环保政策。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhèngzài zhìdìng xīn de huánbǎo zhèngcè.
example.english: The government is drawing up a new environmental policy.
example.fact: The 1987 Montreal Protocol, an international treaty drawn up to phase out ozone-depleting chemicals like CFCs, is considered one of the most successful environmental agreements ever ratified — it achieved universal ratification by all 198 UN member states, and the Antarctic ozone hole has been slowly shrinking as a result.

components.note: 木 (wood) — early spears and rifle stocks were made of wood.
仓 (cāng) is close in sound to qiāng, sharing the same rhyme.
声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.

example.hanzi: 深夜里突然传来一声枪声。
example.pinyin: Shēnyè lǐ tūrán chuánlái yī shēng qiāngshēng.
example.english: A gunshot suddenly rang out in the dead of night.
example.fact: A gunshot's characteristic crack is partly a sonic boom: many bullets travel faster than the speed of sound (about 343 meters per second at sea level), so the sharp noise people hear is a small shockwave, distinct from and often louder than the muzzle blast of the gun itself.

components.note: 生 (growth, a sprout) — the fresh color of new plant growth.
丹 (a well, or mineral pigment) — combined with 生 to give 青 its meaning 'blue-green, young, fresh.'
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'

example.hanzi: 越来越多的青年选择自主创业。
example.pinyin: Yuèláiyuè duō de qīngnián xuǎnzé zìzhǔ chuàngyè.
example.english: More and more young people are choosing to start their own businesses.
example.fact: The United Nations defines "youth" as people aged 15 to 24, a group that numbered around 1.2 billion people globally as of the early 2020s — roughly one in every six people on the planet — with the largest concentrations of young people found in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.

components.note: 一 (a line, representing a target or standard) — 正 shows a foot arriving exactly at the right mark.
止 (foot, to stop) — arriving and stopping precisely at the target gives 正 its meaning of 'correct' or 'straight.'
十 (here a straight vertical line) — 直 pictures something drawn perfectly straight.
目 (eye) — looking directly and steadily with the eye gave 直 its meaning 'straight' or 'direct.'

example.hanzi: 大家都很信任他，因为他为人正直。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu hěn xìnrèn tā, yīnwèi tā wéirén zhèngzhí.
example.english: Everyone trusts him because he is an honest and upright person.
example.fact: A 2019 study published in Science dropped over 17,000 "lost" wallets containing varying amounts of cash in more than 40 countries and found that people were, on average, more likely to report and return a wallet containing money than one without — a result that surprised even the researchers who ran the experiment.

components.note: 寸 (a hand) — a hand at work below.
叀, an old pictograph of a spindle, sits above — spinning thread by hand required focused, single-minded effort, the source of 专's meaning 'specialized, single-minded, exclusively.'
氵 (water) — 注 relates to pouring or directing, like water poured into something
主 (zhǔ) is close in sound to 注's reading zhù

example.hanzi: 她工作时非常专注，很少被打扰。
example.pinyin: Tā gōngzuò shí fēicháng zhuānzhù, hěn shǎo bèi dǎrǎo.
example.english: She is extremely focused when working and is rarely disturbed.
example.fact: Psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi coined the term "flow" in the 1970s to describe the state of deep, focused absorption in a task where a person loses track of time. His research found that flow is most likely to occur when a task's difficulty closely matches a person's skill level — too easy causes boredom, too hard causes anxiety.
